Q: Various places to configure httpclient timeout in Spring boot A:

As in: RestTemplate is not a wrapper around Apache HttpClient. It should also support the JDK HttpClient, OkHttpClient, the old URLConnection and probably some others as well I am not remembering. Whatever configuration RestTemplate exposes through its public API must be cross-compatible. Consistency is, ironically, why you are seeing less configuration properties.

Q: Sorting List randomly by weights A:

I’m returning to this years later because I finally found the mathematical explanation for why my initial approach was failing and how to achieve a "one-pass" weighted sort correctly. The non-linearity observed (the 85-13-2% skew) occurred because multiplying a weight by a linear random value (R x W) does not result in a true weighted permutation. It disproportionately favors the highest weights. To achieve the correct distribution in a single sort, you actually need to use the Efraimidis-Spirakis algorithm. The correct formula for the sort key is ki = ui1/wi (where u is a random value between 0 and 1, and w is the weight).

I recently did a deep dive into the math behind this and wrote a detailed explanation of the implementation in C#. This algorithm allows for an O(N log N) complexity and works beautifully even for streaming data where you don't know the full list size upfront. You can find the full breakdown and the corrected code here: The Weight of Decisions: Solving Weighted Random Sorting at Scale.

Q: I cannot access my localhost from my iphone A:

It's very easy. At least for me.

  1. Connect the iPhone Via USB (This does not work on wireless debugging)

  2. Go to Settings > Search Sharing and at the bottom, there is your Mac Local host name. yourname-MacBook-Air.local

  3. Test it on the iPhone Safari, go to yourname-MacBook-Air.local:port replace port with your server port. Mine was 8080

Alternative:

echo "$(scutil --get LocalHostName).local:8080"

It works:

  • no need to enable hotspot on either on the devices,
  • no need to configure any proxy,
  • no need to configure internet sharing whatsoever
  • No need to have internet at all on both the device. This works offline
  • No need to be on the same wifi network

On Android, I use ADB reverse tcp.

Q: Get unique elements in multiple List columns A:

If you want to stay inside Polars (avoiding to_list() and Python-side loops), you can do it entirely with expressions. You can just explode both columns, stack and then unique.

import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [range(1, 3), range(5, 10)],
    "b": [range(4, 9), range(6, 11)],
})

unique_vals = (
    df
    .select(pl.all().explode()) 
    .melt(value_name="val")       
    .select(pl.col("val").unique())
    .to_series()
    .to_list()
)
# -> [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Or you can try Concatenate lists row-wise, explode, then unique.

unique_vals = (
    df
    .select(pl.concat_list("a", "b").alias("lists")) 
    .select(pl.col("lists").arr.explode().alias("val"))
    .select(pl.col("val").unique())
    .to_series()
    .to_list()
)

In reality, kindly keep in mind that staying in Polars (using explode, melt, and unique) is typically much faster and memory efficient than building Python lists and set-comprehensions, especially for large data sets. Hope it gives you clarity.
